name: MCL — deep (meniscofemoral/meniscotibial)
description: Thickening of the medial capsule (layer 3) beneath the superficial MCL: a longer meniscofemoral part to the upper rim of the meniscal body and a short meniscotibial (coronary) part from its lower rim to the tibia. Thin low-signal bands above and below the meniscus on coronal images, inseparable from its rim.
variants_pitfalls: A thin, sharp fat or fluid line between the layers is normal. Call a tear on discontinuous fibers or joint fluid tracking between the deep and superficial layers. The meniscofemoral part tears far more often (93% vs 6% in one ACL series).
MCL bursitis: fluid between the layers, often in separate parts above and below the meniscus, with intact ligaments and meniscus; a parameniscal cyst instead connects to a meniscal tear.
Meniscocapsular separation is overcalled (positive predictive value 9% medially in one series); reserve it for fluid clearly separating the meniscus from both deep MCL parts in an injured knee.
Deep MCL injury (31% of clinically isolated ACL ruptures in one series) is linked to ramp lesions: check the posterior horn's capsular junction.
